question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{5x}.$ Its derivative is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=5(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{5x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$

current_example.problem: Find the derivative of the function $y = (\sin x)^{\cos x}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y = (\sin x)^{\cos x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $y'{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y = (\sin x)^{\cos x}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x))\end{aligned}
$$
